earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only wordlists (Blench 2006, Koops 1971, Benue-Congo comparative lists); no grammar or phonology of Batu exists.

sources.citation: OLAC listing for btu (archived 2025) and Glottolog 5.x languoid page batu1255
sources.note: Bibliographic check only: OLAC lists nothing but Glottolog and Ethnologue entries; Glottolog has zero grammar/phonology/sketch references (only overviews and wordlists: Piron 1997, Williamson 1973, Williamson & Shimizu 1968, Wente-Lukas 1985, Meek 1931, Blench 2006, 2016).

sources.citation: Angitso, Michael T. & Roland Kiessling. 2024. Towards reconstructing the numeral classifier system of Proto-Tivoid. Afrika und Uebersee 97: 204-232. doi:10.15460/auue.2024.97.1.329
sources.note: Checked for new Batu sources: contains no Batu data and cites no Batu description (Tiv, Ugare, Iyive etc. only); nothing on stress. Not retained held by the project.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2024. An overview of the Bantoid languages. Afrika und Übersee 97: 1-46. Hamburg University Press. doi:10.15460/auue.2024.97.1.288 (CC-BY).
sources.note: Name only (Greenberg figure); Tivoid tone entries are for Ugarə (H, L, upstep, downstep) and Esimbi, not Batu.

sources.citation: Akombo, Elijah I., Lawan Jafaru Tahir & Danga Liatu. 2023. Historical Account of the Origin, Migration and Transformation of the Tigun Society in Kurmi Local Government Area. Labar: Journal of Military History & Peace Studies (Nigerian Army University, Biu) 3(2), June 2023: 153-165 (approx.).
sources.note: Nothing on the sound system. Only language-related content: 'The Batu is also another category of the Tigun with a completely different dialect as well' and Table one listing Batu (Boko) villages Batu Amanda, Batu Affih, Batu Kamino. No transcription, tone or stress remarks; the one 'stresses' hit is the verb ('Usman further stresses that Kurmi..').

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2016. New research on Tivoid and its place within Bantoid. Slides presented at Bantu 6, University of Helsinki, 20-22 June 2016.
sources.note: Nothing; Batu mentioned only for classification/population; mentions tonal alternation in Tivoid verb/noun morphology generally (Iyive, Iceve), not Batu.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. [2016]. The Tivoid languages: Overview and Comparative Word List. Circulation draft, ms. (Glottolog ref 78922)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; Batu appears only in the classification history and Table 1 (source: Koops ms.). Only prosodic remark is that Tiv and Ugare are two-tone languages and Esimbi has three tones; Batu not mentioned there.

sources.citation: Starr, Alan & Clark Regnier. 2008 [1990]. Tivoid survey. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2008-022.
sources.note: No Batu content at all (Cameroon-side Tivoid only); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2006 [printout Nov. 2010]. Wordlists of Batu, Kamino and Buru languages spoken in southern Taraba State, Nigeria. Data collected by Robert Koops in the 1970s, typed by Emma Connell, revised and converted to Unicode by R. Blench. Ms., Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, Cambridge. 14 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Two-page intro (classification only) plus a tone-marked comparative wordlist (Afi/Amanda, Kamino, Buru, Manta, Tiv). Intro p.1 notes: 'Robert Koops also prepared a typescript on Batu phonemes, which I hope to incorporate in a later version.'

sources.citation: Chan, Eugene S. L. (compiler). 2006-2023. Numeral Systems of the World's Languages [per-language data pages with contributor, date and comments]. Leipzig: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology, Department of Linguistics.https://lingweb.eva.mpg.de/channumerals/(pages: Kwaja.htm - data Greg McLean, SIL Cameroon, 7 Apr 2013; Somyev.htm - Bruce Connell, 17 Aug 2007; Kapya.htm - Tamara Prischnegg, 15 Apr 2013; Dugun.htm - Lars Lode, EELC, 14 Nov 1994; Abon.htm, Batu.htm, Bitare.htm - second-hand from Mark Rosenfelder, 7 Oct 2023; Mfumte.htm - Domche Teko Engelbert, 1996, Koffa dialect).

sources.note: Untoned 1-10 list (dɪfu, ɛ-vu, tare, nai, tšun.. gbue); nothing on tone or stress.

sources.citation: Koops, Robert. n.d. [1970s]. Batu phonemes. Unpublished typescript (referred to in Blench 2006:1: 'Robert Koops also prepared a typescript on Batu phonemes').
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only known phonological analysis of Batu; if it has a suprasegmentals section it would be the sole first-hand statement on tone/stress. Possibly held by R. Blench (Kay Williamson Educational Foundation) or in Koops's papers (SIL Nigeria / NBTT, Jos).

sources.citation: Meek, Charles K. 1931. Tribal Studies in Northern Nigeria. 2 vols. London: Kegan Paul, Trench, Trubner. Vol. II pp. 565-569, 586-589 (Batu notes and vocabulary).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Earliest record of Batu; short vocabulary with possible transcription notes; very unlikely to state a stress rule but is the only other primary source.

sources.citation: Koops, Robert. 1971. Wordlists from the linguistic survey of the Baissa area. Unpublished survey report, SUM(CRC) [Sudan United Mission, Christian Reformed Church branch], Nigeria. 69 pp. (Glottolog ref 703244; lists for Batu Amanda, Afi/Amanda and Kamino = Batu [btu], with Mashi, Bukwen, Abon and Bitare.)
sources.tag: likely states tone; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: in print; no library copy located
sources.note: A survey wordlist, not a tone analysis; Koops's Batu/Kamino forms as retyped in Blench 2006 are tone-marked with grave, macron and acute diacritics (e.g. nàdì 'stone', tòwā 'hard', ŋ̀wàn 'grinding stone'), so the original very likely carries tone-marked transcriptions and possibly a transcription/phoneme note, but no prose tone statement is expected.

tone.says: A survey wordlist, not a tone analysis; Koops's Batu/Kamino forms as retyped in Blench 2006 are tone-marked with grave, macron and acute diacritics (e.g. nàdì 'stone', tòwā 'hard', ŋ̀wàn 'grinding stone'), so the original very likely carries tone-marked transcriptions and possibly a transcription/phoneme note, but no prose tone statement is expected.
